name: OpenWeather
description: OpenWeather current conditions by location — temperature, humidity, wind, conditions. Pay-per-call x402.

city.description: City name (e.g. London, Tokyo, New York)

usage.callShape: GET https://openweather-coral.vercel.app/weather/current?lat=51.5&lon=-0.12 (x402, USDC on Base $0.002). Pass lat & lon as query params.
usage.outputShape: body.city, body.country, body.temperature.{current,feels_like,min,max,unit}, body.humidity, body.pressure, body.wind.{speed,direction,gust}, body.weather.{main,description,icon}, body.clouds, body.sunrise, body.sunset, body.updated_at
quirks: The documented ?city=<name> query param is BROKEN: it returns HTTP 500 (HTML 'Internal Server Error') after the payment flow even though the unpaid pre-flight shows 402. Server-side city-name geocoding fails. Use ?lat=&lon= instead — that variant works reliably.
Pass lat/lon as query-string params on the GET (not a JSON body).
Response city field reflects the resolved locality (e.g. lat 51.5/lon -0.12 -> 'City of Westminster'), not necessarily the nearest major city name.
usage.guide: Call GET https://openweather-coral.vercel.app/weather/current with ?lat=<latitude>&lon=<longitude> query params; payment is x402 USDC on Base (~$0.002). Do NOT use the ?city= param — it is documented but returns a 500 server error. Read current conditions from the JSON body: body.temperature.current (celsius), body.humidity, body.wind.speed/direction, and body.weather.main / body.weather.description for the textual condition.

name: Precip AI
description: Precip AI hyperlocal weather — current conditions and short-term hyperlocal precipitation/forecast data. Pay-per-call x402 via Orthogonal.

lat.description: Latitude coordinate (-90 to 90) for the location center of the precipitation widget

lon.description: Longitude coordinate (-180 to 180) for the location center of the precipitation widget

apiKey.description: Your API key for authentication. Gets automatically applied as header.

units.description: Unit system for displaying precipitation amounts and temperatures. 'metric' shows mm and °C, 'imperial' shows inches and °F.

widgets.description:
Comma-separated list of widget keys to display.

Available options:
`current`, `event`, `calendar`, `cumulative`, `total`, `precip`, `table`, `wind`, `temp`, `soiltemp`, `soilmoisture`, `snow`

When not provided, shows all widgets.

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.orth.sh/precip/embed/location?lat={lat}&lon={lon}&units=metric&widgets=current,temp,precip (x402-paid, no apiKey supplied by caller)
usage.outputShape: Response body is a full text/html document (the Precip embed widget SPA page, ~6KB), NOT JSON. The weather data is rendered client-side inside this embeddable widget page; there is no JSON dot-path. Treat body as an HTML widget to iframe/render.
quirks: Returns text/html (an embeddable widget SPA page), NOT JSON weather data — an agent expecting structured precip/temp values will not find them in the raw response; the data is rendered client-side.
The inputSchema lists apiKey as required, but the caller does NOT supply it — the x402 gateway auto-applies the apiKey header after payment. Do not pass apiKey.
lat and lon are required query params; units (metric/imperial, default metric) and widgets (comma-separated keys like current,temp,precip; defaults to all) are optional.
This is the /embed/location route — it serves an HTML widget for embedding, not a data API.
usage.guide: Call GET https://x402.orth.sh/precip/embed/location with required lat and lon query params (e.g. lat=42.378792&lon=-83.7935); add optional units (metric|imperial) and widgets (comma-separated: current,event,calendar,cumulative,total,precip,table,wind,temp,soiltemp,soilmoisture,snow). Pay via x402 (~$0.10 USDC on Base) — do NOT pass the apiKey param, the gateway injects it after payment. The 200 response is a text/html embeddable widget page, not JSON; use it by embedding/rendering the HTML (iframe), since the weather values are rendered client-side rather than returned as structured data.

name: 2s.io Weather
description: Weather by US ZIP code — current conditions lookup. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/weather/zip?zip=10001
usage.outputShape: body.data.items[0].location {zip,city,state,coords{lat,lon},timezone} and body.data.items[0].current {temperatureF,apparentTemperatureF,humidityPct,windMph,windDirection,windDirectionDeg,precipProbabilityPct,conditions,isDay,observedAt}; body.data.source attributes NOAA; settlement at body.meta.settlement
quirks: Result is nested under body.data.items[] (an array even for a single ZIP) — read items[0]
zip is a query-string param, not a path segment
US ZIPs only (NOAA-backed)
usage.guide: Call GET https://2s.io/api/weather/zip with a query parameter zip set to a 5-digit US ZIP code (e.g. ?zip=10001). It is an x402 paid endpoint at ~$0.0012 USDC on Base (also accepts Solana USDC). The response is synchronous JSON; read current conditions from body.data.items[0].current and location metadata from body.data.items[0].location. Data is sourced from NOAA, so only US ZIPs work.

name: Hugen Weather Current
description: Get current weather conditions for any city worldwide (temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind, precipitation, condition). No API keys, no geocoding setup. Pass a city name or explicit lat/lon.

usage.callShape: GET https://weather.hugen.tokyo/weather/current?city=Tokyo  (alternatively ?lat=35.6895&lon=139.69 — supply either city OR lat+lon; all params technically optional)
usage.outputShape: city, country, latitude, longitude, temperature_c, feels_like_c, humidity_pct, wind_speed_kmh, wind_direction_deg, precipitation_mm, condition, weather_code, observation_time
quirks: Query params only (GET); no request body.
Provide either `city` OR `lat`+`lon`. Params are nominally optional but a location is needed for useful results.
Temperatures in Celsius, wind in km/h, precipitation in mm.
`condition` is a human string (e.g. 'Mainly clear') and `weather_code` is the numeric WMO code (e.g. 1).
`observation_time` is an ISO local timestamp without timezone offset (e.g. 2026-06-11T01:00).
Keyless x402 on Base, $0.01 flat per call.
usage.guide: Get current weather conditions for any city worldwide (temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind, precipitation, condition). No API keys, no geocoding setup. Pass a city name or explicit lat/lon. GET https://weather.hugen.tokyo/weather/current?city=Tokyo  (alternatively ?lat=35.6895&lon=139.69 — supply either city OR lat+lon; all params technically optional) Output: city, country, latitude, longitude, temperature_c, feels_like_c, humidity_pct, wind_speed_kmh, wind_direction_deg, precipitation_mm, condition, weather_code, observation_time

name: Hugen Weather Forecast
description: Get a daily weather forecast (1-7 days) for any city worldwide. Returns per-day max/min temperature, condition, precipitation amount + probability, and max wind. No API keys.

usage.callShape: GET https://weather.hugen.tokyo/weather/forecast?city=Tokyo&days=3  (alternatively ?lat=..&lon=..; days defaults to 3, range 1-7)
usage.outputShape: city, country, latitude, longitude, days[].{date, condition, weather_code, temp_max_c, temp_min_c, precipitation_mm, precipitation_probability_pct, wind_max_kmh}
quirks: Query params only (GET); no request body.
Provide either `city` OR `lat`+`lon`.
`days` is an integer 1-7, default 3; values >7 are rejected by schema (max 7).
Forecast data lives in a `days[]` array (one object per date), unlike /weather/current which returns a flat snapshot.
Per-day fields: temp_max_c/temp_min_c (C), precipitation_mm + precipitation_probability_pct, wind_max_kmh, plus condition string and numeric WMO weather_code.
Keyless x402 on Base, $0.01 flat per call regardless of days requested.
usage.guide: Get a daily weather forecast (1-7 days) for any city worldwide. Returns per-day max/min temperature, condition, precipitation amount + probability, and max wind. No API keys. GET https://weather.hugen.tokyo/weather/forecast?city=Tokyo&days=3  (alternatively ?lat=..&lon=..; days defaults to 3, range 1-7) Output: city, country, latitude, longitude, days[].{date, condition, weather_code, temp_max_c, temp_min_c, precipitation_mm, precipitation_probability_pct, wind_max_kmh}

name: Japan Weather (JMA)
description: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) weather forecast data for Japanese locations. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: GET https://weather.agentic-jp.com/forecast/:area where :area is a JMA 6-digit area code (e.g. 130000 for Tokyo). No body, no query params.
usage.outputShape: body.summary_en (one-line English summary), body.daily[] (today/tomorrow: .weather_en, .pops[], .temps[]), body.weekly[] (7-day: .weather_en, .pop, .temp_min, .temp_max, .reliability), body.area.name_en, body.report_datetime
quirks: The :area path segment must be a JMA 6-digit area-office code, NOT a city name or lat/long. 130000 = Tokyo. Other examples: 016000=Sapporo, 270000=Osaka, 400000=Fukuoka, 471000=Okinawa.
Japan-only coverage (Japan Meteorological Agency data).
Response mixes Japanese and English fields; use the *_en fields (weather_en, name_en, summary_en) for English. Raw weather/wind/wave strings and summary_ja are Japanese.
Plain sync x402 on Base ($0.003 USDC); no auth, no async.
usage.guide: Pick a JMA 6-digit area code for the Japanese location you want (130000=Tokyo, 270000=Osaka, 016000=Sapporo, 400000=Fukuoka, 471000=Okinawa) and GET https://weather.agentic-jp.com/forecast/{code}. It is a paid x402 endpoint (~$0.003 USDC on Base), no body or auth required. Read body.summary_en for a quick English answer, body.daily[] for today/tomorrow (weather_en, pops percent-chance-of-rain array, temps array), and body.weekly[] for the 7-day outlook (weather_en, pop, temp_min, temp_max). Japan only.

name: x402-deployer Weather
description: Current weather lookup by location. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev/weather with JSON body {latitude:number, longitude:number}
usage.outputShape: body.current.temperature, body.current.humidity_pct, body.current.wind_speed, body.current.weather_code; body.daily[] (per-day temperature_max/min, precipitation_mm, sunrise, sunset, uv_index_max); body.location.{lat,lon,timezone,elevation_m}; body.units, body.source
quirks: Input MUST be numeric latitude/longitude (e.g. {"latitude":37.77,"longitude":-122.42}); a {"location":"San Francisco"} string is rejected with 400 'latitude must be a number in [-90,90]' AND STILL CHARGES $0.005. Geocode any place name to coordinates before calling.
latitude must be in [-90,90], longitude in [-180,180].
Output is in metric units (celsius, km/h, mm); data sourced from open-meteo.com.
weather_code is a WMO code (e.g. 0=clear, 3=overcast, 45=fog) - map it client-side.
usage.guide: Call POST https://x402-deployer.x402-deployer.workers.dev/weather with a JSON body of numeric latitude and longitude (geocode any place name first - a location-name string is rejected with a 400 but still charges you). Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base, no auth/SIWX. The 200 response is synchronous JSON: read current conditions from body.current (temperature, humidity_pct, wind_speed, weather_code in WMO codes) and a 3-day forecast from body.daily[]. Units are metric and data comes from open-meteo.

name: Open-Meteo Weather
description: Current weather for a coordinate via Open-Meteo (open-source weather data) — temperature, humidity, wind, precipitation and weather code. Query by ?lat=&lng=. Pay-per-call x402 (Base USDC) served by the x402node gateway.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/maps/weather?lat={lat}&lng={lng} (no body; x402 USDC on Base). Registry says POST but the endpoint is actually GET with query params.
usage.outputShape: body.temperature_c, body.apparent_c, body.humidity_pct, body.precipitation_mm, body.wind_kmh, body.wind_direction_deg, body.weather_code, body.weather_description, body.is_day, body.observation_time, body.timezone, body.elevation_m, body.lat, body.lng
quirks: Registry lists method=POST but the endpoint is actually GET — pass coordinates as URL query params ?lat=&lng=, NO request body.
Param names are lat and lng (not lon/longitude).
Response includes a marketing _hint field that should be ignored.
Times are returned in GMT/UTC (timezone:'GMT').
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.x402node.dev/maps/weather with query params lat and lng (decimal degrees), e.g. ?lat=40.7128&lng=-74.0060. Send no request body — despite the registry listing POST, this is a GET endpoint. Pay $0.01 USDC on Base via x402. The 200 JSON response gives current conditions directly: read temperature_c, humidity_pct, wind_kmh, precipitation_mm, and weather_description. Times are in GMT; ignore the _hint marketing field.

name: x402node Weather Forecast
description: Multi-day daily weather forecast (1-16 days) by city name or lat/lon: per-day high/low temperature, precipitation amount and probability, max wind, and a conditions summary (open-meteo sourced). Pay-per-call x402.

outputSchema.forecast: array of { date, tMaxC, tMinC, precipMm, precipProbPct, windMaxKph, conditions }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/weather/forecast?lat={lat}&lon={lon}&days={n} (or ?city={name}&days={n}). No request body; x402 USDC on Base $0.005.
usage.outputShape: body.location.{lat,lon}, body.days, body.forecast[].{date, tMaxC (°C max), tMinC (°C min), precipMm, precipProbPct, windMaxKph, conditions}, body.note, body.source ('open-meteo')
quirks: Query params only (GET); no request body.
Provide either `city` OR `lat`+`lon`. Param names are lat and lon (not lng/longitude).
`days` is 1-16 (default 7); passed as a string query param.
Temperatures in Celsius (tMaxC/tMinC), wind in km/h (windMaxKph), precipitation in mm; precipProbPct is percent chance of rain.
`conditions` is a human string (e.g. 'heavy rain') that can be 'unknown' for later forecast days.
Response includes a marketing _hint field that should be ignored.
Distinct from x402node's /maps/weather ('Open-Meteo Weather'), which returns CURRENT conditions for a single coordinate.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.x402node.dev/weather/forecast with query params — either lat & lon (decimal degrees, e.g. ?lat=40.7128&lon=-74.006) or city (?city=Tokyo), plus optional days (1-16, default 7). Send no request body. Pay $0.005 USDC on Base via x402 (no auth/SIWX). The 200 JSON is synchronous: read the per-day outlook from body.forecast[] — each entry has date, tMaxC/tMinC (°C), precipMm and precipProbPct (rain amount + chance), windMaxKph, and a conditions summary string. Data is open-meteo sourced; ignore the _hint field.

name: 2s Solar Forecast
description: Daily solar irradiance + PV-yield forecast for any global coordinate (free/keyless upstream, Open-Meteo) — a 1-16 day daily forecast of GHI (kWh/m²), peak sun hours, sunshine hours, and estimated yield per kWp of panels at a 0.75 performance ratio, for rooftop-solar planning, agrivoltaics, and EV-charge scheduling.

days.description: Number of daily forecast days to return (1-16).

total.description: Total matching rows upstream; null when unknown.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/energy/solar-forecast with query params latitude, longitude (required, decimal degrees WGS84) and days (optional, 1-16). Pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana). Result is returned inline in the 200; no polling.
usage.outputShape: data.ok=true; data.items[0] = { latitude, longitude, timezone (IANA or null), performanceRatio (0.75), days[]{date (YYYY-MM-DD), ghiKwhPerM2, peakSunHours, sunshineHours, estYieldKwhPerKwp} }; data.total=1; data.source={provider:'Open-Meteo', url, license}; plus top-level meta.cost.usd and meta.settlement{txHash,network,success}.
quirks: Inputs are QUERY-STRING params (latitude, longitude, days), not a JSON body and not path segments.
Result is nested under body.data.items[] (an array with a single element even for one point) — read items[0], and the per-day forecast from items[0].days[].
Global coverage, keyless upstream: data is sourced from Open-Meteo (attribution in data.source), served through 2s.io's own x402 gateway. estYieldKwhPerKwp assumes a fixed 0.75 performance ratio.

days controls the number of daily forecast days returned (1-16; the OpenAPI parameter description mislabels it 'look-back window', but the endpoint is a forward forecast and the returned dates start today).
Free verification without paying: append ?trial=1 (or header X-2s-Trial:1) for one free real call per endpoint per hour — used here to pre-validate the input before the paid call.
Complements energy.solar-resource (NREL long-run US averages); this endpoint is a short-horizon global forecast.
usage.guide: Get a daily solar forecast for a coordinate. GET https://2s.io/api/energy/solar-forecast?latitude=<lat>&longitude=<lon>&days=<1-16> (latitude/longitude required in decimal degrees; days optional). Pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana, ~$0.00144). Read the forecast from data.items[0].days[] — each day has date, ghiKwhPerM2 (global horizontal irradiance), peakSunHours, sunshineHours, and estYieldKwhPerKwp (estimated PV yield per kWp at a 0.75 performance ratio). Global coverage; data is from Open-Meteo. Verified 2026-07-30 with {latitude:37.7749,longitude:-122.4194,days:3} → HTTP 200, $0.00144 charged.

name: 2s Sunrise
description: Compute sunrise, sunset, solar noon, and civil/nautical/astronomical twilight times (ISO-8601 UTC) plus day length for a given latitude/longitude and date, using the NOAA Solar Calculator (Meeus algorithms) computed locally.

sunrise.description: ISO-8601 UTC; null at high latitudes during polar day/night.

notes.description: Notes, e.g. polar day/night when an event does not occur.

usage.callShape: GET https://2s.io/api/sunrise/compute?lat={lat}&lon={lon}&date={YYYY-MM-DD} — no body; pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana). Result returned inline in the 200; no polling.
usage.outputShape: data.ok=true; data.items[0] = { sunrise, sunset, solarNoon, civilTwilightBegin/End, nauticalTwilightBegin/End, astronomicalTwilightBegin/End (all ISO-8601 UTC, or null during polar day/night), dayLengthMinutes (number), notes[] }; data.total=1; data.source={provider:'NOAA Solar Calculator (Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms 2nd ed.) — computed locally', url, license:'Public domain (US government work)'}; data.meta.query echoes {latitude,longitude,date}; plus top-level meta.cost.usd and meta.settlement{txHash,network}.
quirks: All three query params (lat -90..90, lon -180..180, date YYYY-MM-DD) are REQUIRED; lat/lon are query params, not path segments.
All returned times are ISO-8601 UTC — convert to the location's local timezone yourself (the API does not localize).
At high latitudes near the solstices an event may not occur (polar day/night): those fields return null and an explanation is added to items[0].notes[].
dayLengthMinutes is the sunrise→sunset interval in minutes.
Read the single result from data.items[0] (items[] is always length 1 for one coordinate+date).
Deterministic local computation from the NOAA Solar Calculator (Meeus algorithms) — no external upstream call; works worldwide, not US-only.
Free verification without paying: append &trial=1 (or header X-2s-Trial:1) for one free real call per endpoint per hour — used here to pre-validate before the paid call.
usage.guide: Compute solar event times for a place and date. GET https://2s.io/api/sunrise/compute with required query params lat, lon (decimal degrees, WGS84) and date (YYYY-MM-DD); no request body. Pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana, ~$0.001) — the pay layer handles the 402. Read the result from data.items[0]: sunrise, sunset, solarNoon, and civil/nautical/astronomical twilight begins/ends are ISO-8601 UTC strings (convert to local time yourself), dayLengthMinutes is the day length, and notes[] flags polar day/night when a field is null. Verified 2026-07-30 with {lat:40.7128, lon:-74.0060, date:'2026-07-30'} → HTTP 200, $0.001 charged (tx 0xb3ec47…).

name: OttoAI Weather
description: Live current weather plus a 5-day forecast for any city (auto-geocoded) or lat/lon worldwide — temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind, conditions and daily highs/lows with precipitation probability. Pay-per-call x402.

inputSchema.location: string (required, query param) — city name (e.g. "Tokyo", "London", "São Paulo") which auto-geocodes, OR a "lat,lon" pair (e.g. "51.5,-0.12")

data.daily: array of { date, maxC, minC, conditions, precipProbPct } (5-day)

usage.callShape: GET https://x402.ottoai.services/weather?location=London (x402, USDC on Base/Polygon/Solana, $0.001). Pass a single `location` query param — a city name (auto-geocoded) or a 'lat,lon' pair. No request body.
usage.outputShape: body.status ('success'); body.data.{location, resolvedName, country, lat, lon}; body.data.current.{tempC, feelsLikeC, humidityPct, windKph, conditions, observedAt}; body.data.daily[].{date, maxC, minC, conditions, precipProbPct} (5-day forecast); body.data.generatedAt; body.meta.{generatedAt, validUntil, stalenessSec, degraded, sourceHealth, inputSnapshotId}
quirks: Single query param `location` (GET, no body) — either a city name (auto-geocoded, no coordinates needed, e.g. 'Tokyo') or a 'lat,lon' string (e.g. '51.5,-0.12').
Temperatures in Celsius (tempC/feelsLikeC/maxC/minC), wind in km/h (windKph); precipProbPct is percent chance of precipitation.
Weather data payload lives under body.data (not top-level); the current snapshot is body.data.current and the 5-day outlook is body.data.daily[].
Sourced from Open-Meteo (see body.meta.sourceHealth); refreshed hourly with freshness metadata in body.meta (generatedAt/validUntil/stalenessSec/degraded).
observedAt/date are ISO local timestamps without timezone offset.
Keyless pay-per-call x402 V2: accepts USDC on Base (eip155:8453, plus a Permit2 variant), Polygon (eip155:137, plus Permit2), and Solana. Flat $0.001 per call.
usage.guide: Call GET https://x402.ottoai.services/weather with a single `location` query param — a city name (auto-geocoded, e.g. ?location=London or ?location=Tokyo) or a 'lat,lon' pair (e.g. ?location=51.5,-0.12). No request body or API key. Pay $0.001 USDC via x402 V2 (Base, Polygon, or Solana). The 200 JSON is synchronous: read current conditions from body.data.current (tempC, feelsLikeC, humidityPct, windKph, conditions) and the 5-day forecast from body.data.daily[] (date, maxC, minC, conditions, precipProbPct). Data is Open-Meteo sourced; check body.meta for freshness (validUntil/stalenessSec/degraded).

name: Greeneris Air Quality
description: Hourly air-quality forecasts for any lat/lon worldwide — PM2.5, PM10, ozone, NO2, SO2, CO, European/US AQI, UV index, dust and aerosol optical depth — from the Copernicus CAMS model served by Open-Meteo, returned as parallel time/value arrays with units.

hourly.description: Comma-separated variables among pm2_5, pm10, ozone, nitrogen_dioxide, sulphur_dioxide, carbon_monoxide, european_aqi, us_aqi, uv_index, dust, aerosol_optical_depth

hourly_units.description: Unit for each requested variable (e.g. pm2_5: μg/m³, european_aqi: EAQI)

hourly.description: Parallel arrays keyed by variable name plus a 'time' array (ISO8601), one value per hour

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/air/quality?latitude=<LAT>&longitude=<LON>&hourly=pm2_5,pm10,european_aqi&forecast_days=2 (x402, USDC on Base $0.002)
usage.outputShape: ok (bool), data.{latitude, longitude, forecast_days, hourly_units{<var>:unit}, hourly{time[], <var>[]...}, source}
quirks: latitude and longitude are required query params; hourly (default pm2_5,pm10,european_aqi) and forecast_days (1-7, default 2) are optional.
Available hourly variables: pm2_5, pm10, ozone, nitrogen_dioxide, sulphur_dioxide, carbon_monoxide, european_aqi, us_aqi, uv_index, dust, aerosol_optical_depth.
Output is parallel arrays: data.hourly.time[] plus one same-length array per requested variable; data.hourly_units gives the unit of each.
Coordinates are snapped to the CAMS model grid, so the echoed latitude/longitude differ slightly from the request (e.g. 2.3522 -> 2.3999996).
Data is from Copernicus CAMS via Open-Meteo (CC-BY 4.0) — attribution to open-meteo.com is required; response cached ~1h.
Static price ($0.002), not a dynamic quote.
usage.guide: Get an hourly air-quality forecast for any location. Pass latitude and longitude (WGS84), optionally hourly=<comma-separated variables> (pm2_5, pm10, ozone, nitrogen_dioxide, sulphur_dioxide, carbon_monoxide, european_aqi, us_aqi, uv_index, dust, aerosol_optical_depth; default pm2_5,pm10,european_aqi) and forecast_days (1-7, default 2). e.g. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/air/quality?latitude=48.8566&longitude=2.3522&hourly=pm2_5,pm10,european_aqi&forecast_days=2 -> data.hourly.time[] with parallel per-variable arrays and data.hourly_units for units. $0.002 USDC on Base per call; sourced from Copernicus CAMS via Open-Meteo, cached ~1h.

name: Greeneris French DPE Certificates
description: Official French energy-performance certificates (DPE) for existing dwellings from the ADEME dpe03existant dataset (data.ademe.fr, Licence Ouverte 2.0, anonymised) — search by postal code or address and get energy class A-G, GHG class, primary-energy consumption (kWh/m2/yr), habitable floor area and construction period per certificate. Spots F/G rental-ban units for real-estate due diligence. Keyless over x402. $0.005.

postal_code.description: 5-digit French postal code, e.g. 75011. Provide this OR address.

address.description: Free-text address matched against the BAN address field, e.g. '48 rue de Montreuil Paris'. Provide this OR postal_code.

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/fr/dpe?postal_code=<5-digit postal code>&size=<1-50>  (or ?address=<free-text French address>&size=<1-50>). Provide postal_code OR address; size is optional (default 10, max 50). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key.
usage.outputShape: { ok:true, data:{ query:{ postal_code, address, size }, total_matches, returned, certificates:[{ numero_dpe, date_etablissement_dpe, etiquette_dpe, etiquette_ges, conso_5_usages_par_m2_ep, emission_ges_5_usages_par_m2, surface_habitable_logement, adresse_ban, code_postal_ban, periode_construction, annee_construction?, type_batiment }], source } } — observed postal_code=75011 returned total_matches=55564, e.g. 48 Rue de Montreuil, etiquette_dpe 'D', conso 157 kWh/m2/yr, 63.3 m2, periode_construction '1948-1974'.
quirks: Provide postal_code OR address — both are optional in the schema but at least one is needed to scope the search (postal_code is the cleanest key; address is fuzzy-matched against the official BAN address field).

etiquette_dpe / etiquette_ges are the letter classes A-G; conso_5_usages_par_m2_ep is primary-energy kWh/m2/yr and emission_ges_5_usages_par_m2 is kgCO2eq/m2/yr. F/G units are the rental-ban ('passoire thermique') flag for due diligence.
Certificate fields vary: some records carry annee_construction (integer year), others only periode_construction (band, e.g. 'avant 1948', '1948-1974').
Data is ADEME dpe03existant (existing dwellings only, anonymised, Licence Ouverte 2.0); responses are cached ~24h.
Response payload is wrapped under data{} — read data.certificates[] and data.total_matches, not top-level.
The x402 quote advertises method enum GET|HEAD|DELETE, but this is a read-only data feed — use GET.
usage.guide: Official French energy-performance certificate lookup (ADEME dpe03existant, Licence Ouverte 2.0). name: Greeneris GB Grid Carbon Intensity
description: Carbon intensity (gCO2/kWh) of Great Britain's electricity grid from the official NESO Carbon Intensity API, in half-hour periods with a low/moderate/high index, national or per DNO region with the per-fuel generation mix.

region.description: DNO regionid 1-17 (optional; 13=London). Switches to a regional scope and includes the per-fuel generation mix. Query param.

horizon.description: Forecast window from now (optional). Adds forecast half-hour periods. Query param.

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/gb/carbon?region=13&horizon=fw24h — both query params optional. No params -> current national half-hour; ?horizon=fw24h|fw48h adds forecast periods; ?region=1..17 (13=London) switches to a DNO region and includes the per-fuel generation_mix. No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { scope: 'national'|'regional', region?: { regionid, name, dno }, unit: 'gCO2/kWh', count, periods: [ { from, to, forecast (gCO2/kWh number), index: 'very low'|'low'|'moderate'|'high'|'very high', generation_mix?: { gas, coal, biomass, imports, nuclear, other, hydro, solar, wind } (percentages; regional scope only) } ], source } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { scope: 'regional', region: { regionid: 13, name: 'London', dno: 'UKPN London' }, unit: 'gCO2/kWh', count: 48, periods: [ { from: '2026-07-30T18:00Z', to: '2026-07-30T18:30Z', forecast: 202, index: 'high', generation_mix: { biomass: 4.3, coal: 0, imports: 28.4, gas: 46.3, nuclear: 3, other: 0, hydro: 0.2, solar: 7.6, wind: 10.3 } } ], source: 'Carbon Intensity API, National Energy System Operator (NESO), CC BY 4.0' } }
quirks: region and horizon are optional query params (not path or body). No params returns the current national half-hour period only; horizon=fw24h/fw48h expands to 48/96 forecast periods.
generation_mix (per-fuel percentages) is only present when a region is requested; national scope omits it.
index is a categorical band (very low / low / moderate / high / very high); forecast is the numeric gCO2/kWh value.
Underlying data is the official NESO Carbon Intensity API (CC BY 4.0) — this is a paid x402 gateway over it. 30-min upstream cadence, 30-min cache.
Sibling ops on the same host (e.g. /v1/gb/power-demand, /v1/eu/power-price) are separate services, not variants of this one.
usage.guide: Carbon intensity of Great Britain's electricity grid (NESO Carbon Intensity API, CC BY 4.0). GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/gb/carbon with optional query params: region (DNO regionid 1-17, 13=London — switches to regional scope and adds per-fuel generation_mix) and horizon (fw24h or fw48h — adds forecast half-hour periods). No params returns the current national half-hour. No body, no API key — pay $0.002 USDC on Base via x402. Response: { ok: true, data: { scope, region?, unit: 'gCO2/kWh', count, periods: [ { from, to, forecast, index, generation_mix? } ], source } }. Use for grid decarbonization dashboards, ESG reporting, and carbon-aware scheduling (run loads when index is low). 30-min cache.

name: Greeneris GB Power Demand
description: Near-real-time Great Britain national electricity demand outturn (5-minute MW readings) from the Elexon Insights (BMRS) open data feed, with the latest value plus a configurable history window.

last.description: Optional. Return only the N most recent 5-minute readings (1-500). e.g. last=12 = last hour.

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/gb/power-demand[?last=N] (x402, USDC on Base ~$0.002). No API key. Optional ?last=N (1-500) sets how many recent 5-min readings to return; default returns last 24h (288 points).
usage.outputShape: body.ok (bool); body.data.unit ('MW'); body.data.resolution ('5min'); body.data.count (int); body.data.latest.{time,demand_mw}; body.data.records[].{time,demand_mw} (sorted oldest->newest); body.data.source (Elexon attribution).
quirks: No required input — a bare GET returns the last 24h (288 five-minute points). ?last=N (1-500) narrows the window (e.g. ?last=12 = last hour).
Data is GB national demand outturn only (not per-region); values in MW.
Upstream (Elexon BMRS) updates every ~5 min and the endpoint serves a 5-min cache, so successive calls within a window may return identical data.

Provider self-identifies as 'eu-verify' in the 402/openapi serviceName; the host data.greeneris.io fronts 70+ distinct pay-per-call data endpoints. Attribution to Elexon is required by the source's open-data license (echoed in body.data.source).
usage.guide: Call GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/gb/power-demand to read near-real-time GB national electricity demand. Payment is x402 USDC on Base (~$0.002), no API key needed. Read body.data.latest.demand_mw for the current MW figure, and iterate body.data.records[] (oldest->newest, each {time, demand_mw}) for the recent series. Add ?last=N (1-500) to limit how many 5-minute points come back (default = last 24h / 288 points; last=12 = last hour).

name: Greeneris Global Disasters

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/geo/disasters with optional query params: type (EQ|TC|FL|VO|WF|DR), level (green|orange|red), bbox ('min_lon,min_lat,max_lon,max_lat'). type codes: EQ=earthquake, TC=tropical cyclone, FL=flood, VO=volcano, WF=wildfire, DR=drought; level filter is an exact color match, not a minimum.

usage.guide: All currently active natural-disaster events worldwide, normalized from GDACS (Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System, EC JRC / UN OCHA, CC-BY 4.0, real-time). name: Greeneris Sea State
description: Hourly sea-state forecast (wave height, direction and period, plus separate wind-wave and swell components) for Mediterranean ports or any lat/lon, up to 7 days ahead, from Open-Meteo Marine wave models — with a summary block for sailing go/no-go, port ops and routing.

port.description: Preset Mediterranean port name (e.g. marseille, ajaccio, genoa). 12 presets available; use instead of latitude/longitude.

latitude.description: Marine point latitude (if no port given).

longitude.description: Marine point longitude (if no port given).

max_wave_height_m_24h.description: Max significant wave height (m) over the next 24h.

max_wave_height_m_all.description: Max significant wave height (m) over the full forecast horizon.

first_hours_wave_m.description: Wave height (m) for the first few forecast hours.

hourly_units.description: Units for each hourly field (wave_height m, wave_period s, wave_direction °, etc.).

hourly.description: Parallel arrays keyed by time[]: wave_height[], wave_direction[], wave_period[], wind_wave_height[], swell_wave_height[], swell_wave_period[].

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/sea/state with query params ?port=<preset>&days=<1-7> (or ?latitude=&longitude=&days=) — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base $0.005). Result is returned inline in the 200; no polling.
usage.outputShape: body.ok=true; body.data.location{latitude,longitude,port}; body.data.summary{max_wave_height_m_24h, max_wave_height_m_all, first_hours_wave_m[]}; body.data.hourly_units{time,wave_height,wave_direction,wave_period,wind_wave_height,swell_wave_height,swell_wave_period}; body.data.hourly = parallel arrays keyed by time[] (wave_height[], wave_direction[], wave_period[], wind_wave_height[], swell_wave_height[], swell_wave_period[]); body.data.forecast_days; body.data.source='Open-Meteo Marine (wave models ECMWF/MeteoFrance/DWD, CC-BY 4.0)'.
quirks: Provide EITHER ?port=<preset> OR ?latitude=&longitude= — port takes precedence and resolves to a fixed marine point (e.g. port=marseille -> lat 43.29/lon 5.375). 12 Mediterranean port presets are supported (e.g. marseille, ajaccio, nice, genoa).
?days defaults to 2; range is 1-7. Larger values return longer hourly arrays.
Static price: the unpaid 402 quotes $0.005 and the paid call settled at exactly $0.005 — not dynamic.
Data is hourly and UTC, cached ~1h upstream. summary.max_wave_height_m_24h is a quick sailing go/no-go signal; wind_wave vs swell are broken out separately in the hourly block.
All numeric fields are wave metrics in the units given by data.hourly_units (height m, period s, direction °).
usage.guide: Get an hourly marine wave/sea-state forecast for a Mediterranean port or any coordinate. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/sea/state with ?port=<preset> (e.g. marseille, ajaccio, genoa) OR ?latitude=<lat>&longitude=<lon>, plus optional ?days=<1-7> (default 2). Pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base, static $0.005). For a fast go/no-go read data.summary.max_wave_height_m_24h; for detail, read the parallel hourly arrays under data.hourly (keyed by data.hourly.time[]) — wave_height, wave_direction, wave_period, and separately wind_wave_height and swell_wave_height/swell_wave_period — using data.hourly_units for units. Result is synchronous in the 200; no polling. Verified 2026-07-30 with {port:'marseille', days:2} -> HTTP 200, $0.005 charged.

end.description: End date YYYYMMDD (max 366 days after start). Query param.

usage.guide: Historical daily solar irradiance + weather from NASA POWER for any coordinate. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/solar/history with required query params latitude, longitude, start (YYYYMMDD), end (YYYYMMDD, <=366 days after start) and optional parameters (1-6 comma-separated NASA POWER codes; default ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN,T2M — surface shortwave irradiance in kWh/m2/day and 2m temperature in C; other codes include WS10M wind speed). name: Greeneris Planetary Kp Index
description: Latest 1-minute estimated planetary Kp geomagnetic index from NOAA SWPC, with a boolean storm flag and trailing time series — signals GPS/GNSS degradation, satellite drag, HF blackouts and grid stress.

last.description: Trailing 1-minute values to return in 'series' (query param, optional, 1-60, default 1)

threshold.description: Kp level that sets storm=true (query param, optional, 0-9, default 5 = G1 storm)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/space/kp?last=6&threshold=5 — both query params optional (last defaults to 1, threshold to 5). No body. x402 USDC on Base, no API key; the payment is the auth.
usage.outputShape: { ok: boolean, data: { time_tag, kp_index (int), estimated_kp (float), storm (bool = estimated_kp >= threshold), threshold, series: [{ time_tag, kp_index, estimated_kp }], source } } — e.g. { ok: true, data: { time_tag: '2026-07-30T17:56:00', kp_index: 1, estimated_kp: 0.67, storm: false, threshold: 5, series: [...6 entries...], source: 'NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (services.swpc.noaa.gov), public domain' } }
quirks: Both params are optional query params (not path/body); calling with no params returns the latest single value with last=1, threshold=5.
storm is a derived boolean: estimated_kp >= threshold (default threshold 5 = G1 storm).
Data is 1-minute estimated planetary Kp from NOAA SWPC (public domain), served with a 60s cache — not a manual daily final Kp.
Result payload is wrapped in { ok, data } — the values live under data.*, and the trailing history under data.series.

This is a space-weather / geomagnetic endpoint filed under 'weather'; sibling ops on the same host (e.g. /v1/solar/history, /v1/air/quality, /v1/geo/quakes) are separate services, not variants of this one.
usage.guide: Latest planetary Kp geomagnetic index from NOAA SWPC as normalized JSON. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/space/kp with optional query params last (trailing 1-minute values, 1-60, default 1) and threshold (Kp level that flips storm=true, 0-9, default 5). Read the result from the top-level JSON: in_sfha tells you if the point is in a Special Flood Hazard Area, flood_zone is the FEMA designation (AE, VE, X, ...), static_bfe_ft is the base flood elevation in feet where published, and mapped indicates whether the point fell inside a mapped flood polygon (mapped=false / zone X is a valid minimal-risk result). Data is the FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer via ArcGIS Living Atlas.

name: Agentstools Hazard Risk
description: US location natural-hazard risk profile from the FEMA National Risk Index (public domain) — overall Risk Index score/rating/national percentile, expected annual loss in USD, social vulnerability and community resilience, a per-hazard breakdown across the 18 NRI perils (earthquake, riverine and coastal flooding, wildfire, hurricane, tornado, hail, heat/cold wave, drought, landslide, tsunami and more), plus a nested FEMA flood-zone lookup — for any US address, coordinates, or FIPS. Pay-per-call x402.

location.description: { matched_address, state, state_abbr, state_fips, county, county_fips, tract_fips, level ('tract'|'county'), lat, lon }

composite.description: { risk_score, risk_rating, national_percentile, expected_annual_loss_usd, social_vulnerability, community_resilience }

flood.description: Nested FEMA flood-zone lookup: { lat, lon, in_sfha, flood_zone, zone_subtype, static_bfe_ft, description, mapped, source, disclaimer }

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/hazard/risk?address=<US address> (or ?lat=..&lon=.. or ?fips=<5 or 11 digit>). No request body; x402 USDC on Base $0.02.
usage.outputShape: body.location.{matched_address,state,state_abbr,state_fips,county,county_fips,tract_fips,level,lat,lon}; body.composite.{risk_score,risk_rating,national_percentile,expected_annual_loss_usd,social_vulnerability,community_resilience}; body.hazards[].{code,label,risk_score,rating,annual_frequency,eal_usd} (up to 18 NRI perils); body.flood.{in_sfha,flood_zone,zone_subtype,static_bfe_ft,description,mapped,source}; body.source; body.disclaimer
quirks: Query-string params only (GET); no request body.
Provide ONE of: address (US street address, auto-geocoded), lat+lon, or fips (5-digit county or 11-digit census tract). US coverage only — outside the US returns 404, bad input 400, never 500.
Result granularity is tract-level where available (location.level 'tract'), county fallback otherwise.
Composite scores and national_percentile are 0-100 floats; hazards with no data return rating 'No Rating' with risk_score 0 (a valid result, not an error).
The response embeds a full FEMA flood-zone lookup under body.flood — a point outside any mapped Special Flood Hazard Area is a valid result (in_sfha false, zone X, mapped false).

Sourced entirely from public-domain US-government data (FEMA National Risk Index via FEMA ArcGIS Online, dated December 2025); risk indicators for informational due-diligence, not insurance/engineering/legal advice.
Static price ($0.02), Base USDC only (no Solana option).
usage.guide: Get a one-call US natural-hazard risk profile for a location from the FEMA National Risk Index. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/hazard/risk with a query param — either address (US street address, e.g. ?address=1 World Way, Los Angeles, CA, auto-geocoded), lat & lon (decimal degrees), or fips (5-digit county or 11-digit census-tract code). The 200 JSON is synchronous: read body.composite for the overall Risk Index score/rating/national_percentile, expected_annual_loss_usd, social_vulnerability and community_resilience; body.hazards[] for the per-peril breakdown (code, label, risk_score, rating, annual_frequency, eal_usd across the 18 NRI hazards); and body.flood for the nested FEMA flood-zone lookup (in_sfha, flood_zone, static_bfe_ft). US coverage only. Verified 2026-08-07 with {address:'1 World Way, Los Angeles, CA'} -> HTTP 200, $0.02 charged (composite risk_score 98.75 'Very High').

name: Agentstools Seismic Design Values
description: USGS ASCE 7 seismic design values for any US point (coordinate or auto-geocoded street address): mapped spectral accelerations Ss/S1, site-modified SMS/SM1, design SDS/SD1, seismic design category, PGA and TL, with selectable ASCE 7 reference document, occupancy risk category, and soil site class. Pay-per-call x402.

address.description: US street address (auto-geocoded; alternative to lat/lon)

ss.description: Mapped MCE_R spectral response acceleration at short periods (g)

s1.description: Mapped MCE_R spectral response acceleration at 1s period (g)

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/hazard/seismic?lat=34.05&lon=-118.24 (or ?address=<US street address>; optionally &ref_doc=asce7-22&risk_category=II&site_class=D). No request body; x402 USDC on Base $0.005.
usage.outputShape: body.{ss, s1, sms, sm1, sds, sd1} spectral accelerations in g; body.seismic_design_category (A-F); body.pga (g); body.tl_sec (long-period transition, seconds); body.reference_document (e.g. 'ASCE7-22'); body.risk_category; body.site_class; body.source; body.disclaimer; body.lat; body.lon.
quirks: Query-string params only (GET); no request body.
Provide either lat+lon OR a US address (auto-geocoded). US coverage only (USGS ASCE 7 building-codes web service).
ref_doc enum: asce7-22 (default), asce7-16, asce7-10; risk_category enum I/II/III/IV (default II); site_class enum A/B/C/D/E/default (default D).
Spectral values (ss/s1/sms/sm1/sds/sd1/pga) are in units of g; tl_sec is in seconds.
Response includes site-modified sms/sm1 and tl_sec beyond the provider's schema example, plus a disclaimer that these are informational due-diligence values, not engineering/insurance/legal advice.
Static price ($0.005), Base USDC only (no Solana option).

name: Greeneris River Discharge
description: Daily river discharge forecast (m³/s) for any river point worldwide, up to 210 days out, from the Copernicus GloFAS model (5 km grid) served via the Open-Meteo Flood API — for flood risk, inland shipping (Rhine/Danube) and hydropower planning.

latitude.description: Latitude of a point on a river in decimal degrees (-90..90)

longitude.description: Longitude of a point on a river in decimal degrees (-180..180)

daily_units.description: Unit for each daily field (e.g. time: iso8601, river_discharge: m³/s)

daily.description: Parallel arrays: a 'time' array (ISO8601 dates) plus one same-length array per requested variable (e.g. river_discharge)

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/hydro/river?latitude=<LAT>&longitude=<LON>&forecast_days=7 (x402, USDC on Base $0.005)
usage.outputShape: ok (bool), data.{latitude, longitude, daily_units{time, river_discharge}, daily{time[], river_discharge[]...}, source}
quirks: latitude and longitude are required query params (a point ON a river); daily (default river_discharge; also river_discharge_max) and forecast_days (1-210, default 7) are optional.
Output is parallel arrays: data.daily.time[] (ISO8601 dates) plus one same-length array per requested variable; data.daily_units gives the unit (river_discharge in m³/s).
Coordinates are snapped to the GloFAS 5 km grid, so the echoed latitude/longitude differ slightly from the request (e.g. 45.75 -> 45.775, 4.85 -> 4.8750153).
Data is from the Copernicus GloFAS model via the Open-Meteo Flood API (CC-BY 4.0) — attribution required; response cached ~6h.
Static price ($0.005), confirmed by both the live 402 quote (accepts.amount 5000 atomic USDC) and the actual paid call.
usage.guide: Get a daily river-discharge forecast for any river location. Pass latitude and longitude (WGS84 decimal degrees) of a point on the river; optionally daily=<comma-separated variables> (default river_discharge; also river_discharge_max) and forecast_days (1-210, default 7). e.g. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/hydro/river?latitude=45.75&longitude=4.85&forecast_days=7 -> data.daily.time[] with a parallel river_discharge[] (m³/s) array and data.daily_units for units. $0.005 USDC on Base per call; sourced from Copernicus GloFAS via Open-Meteo Flood API, cached ~6h. Useful for flood risk, inland shipping (Rhine/Danube) and hydropower planning.

name: Greeneris Weather Forecast
description: Hourly weather forecast (up to 16 days) for any lat/lon worldwide — temperature, precipitation, wind and ~80 other variables plus optional daily aggregates — from Open-Meteo (blend of ECMWF/GFS/ICON models), returned as parallel ISO8601 time/value arrays with units.

hourly.description: Comma-separated hourly variables (~80 available, e.g. temperature_2m, precipitation, wind_speed_10m, relative_humidity_2m, cloud_cover, ...)

hourly_units.description: Unit for each requested variable (e.g. temperature_2m: °C, precipitation: mm, wind_speed_10m: km/h)

hourly.description: Parallel arrays keyed by variable name plus a 'time' array (ISO8601), one value per hour

usage.callShape: GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/wx/forecast?latitude=<LAT>&longitude=<LON>&hourly=temperature_2m,precipitation,wind_speed_10m&forecast_days=2 (x402, USDC on Base $0.001)
usage.outputShape: ok (bool), data.{latitude, longitude, elevation_m, timezone, hourly_units{<var>:unit}, hourly{time[], <var>[]...}, source}
quirks: latitude and longitude are required query params; hourly (default temperature_2m,precipitation,wind_speed_10m), forecast_days (1-16, default 2), daily (optional aggregates) and timezone (default UTC, or 'auto') are optional.
Output is parallel arrays: data.hourly.time[] plus one same-length array per requested variable; data.hourly_units gives the unit of each.
Coordinates are snapped to the model grid, so the echoed latitude/longitude differ slightly from the request (e.g. 2.3522 -> 2.3599997).
Data is from Open-Meteo (blend of ECMWF/GFS/ICON models, CC-BY 4.0) — attribution to open-meteo.com is required; response cached ~15 min.
Static price ($0.001), not a dynamic quote — one transient 402 read returned $0.002 but three serial reads and the actual paid call all confirmed $0.001.
usage.guide: Get an hourly weather forecast for any location. Pass latitude and longitude (WGS84 decimal degrees), optionally hourly=<comma-separated variables> (~80 available; default temperature_2m,precipitation,wind_speed_10m), forecast_days (1-16, default 2), daily=<comma-separated aggregates>, and timezone (IANA name or 'auto', default UTC). e.g. GET https://data.greeneris.io/v1/wx/forecast?latitude=48.8566&longitude=2.3522&hourly=temperature_2m,precipitation,wind_speed_10m&forecast_days=2 -> data.hourly.time[] with parallel per-variable arrays and data.hourly_units for units. $0.001 USDC on Base per call; sourced from Open-Meteo, cached ~15 min.
